A macro records the commands you run (menus, buttons, shortcuts, gestures) and runs them again in order. Strokes drawn by hand are not recorded.
The artwork you edited last; tap to open it
Pinch with two fingers to zoom, drag them to move and twist them to rotate. A quick pinch fits the artwork to the screen.
Tap with two fingers to undo and with three to redo; keep them down to repeat. The arrows at the side do the same.
The brush at the top opens the library. Smudge and eraser use brushes too, each its own. The sliders at the side set the size and the opacity.
The layers button opens the panel: add layers, drag them into order, hide them, and change their blend mode and opacity.
The circle at the top right opens the colors. Touch and hold the canvas with a finger to pick a color from the artwork.
Smudge drags the colors under the pen, with the shape of the smudge brush.
The eraser removes paint with the shape of its own brush. The pen’s eraser end erases too.
Draw the area to work on; the bar below chooses how. Painting and adjustments then stay inside it.
Drag the box and its handles to move, scale and rotate; the bar below has the other modes.
The pen paints with colors copied from the clone source shown on the canvas.
Drag the edges and corners of the box to choose what stays.
Drag left or right across the canvas to change the amount; tap for the options.
Drag the guide’s handles to place it. Nothing is painted while you edit it.
Tap the canvas to place a text box, or tap a text layer to edit it.
Introduction and tips on their own
Nanquim is free and open source, with no paid features and no ads. It is made by people who give their time; donations pay for devices to test on and for the project’s costs.
The project has no donation page yet. Thank you for wanting to help!
